name: AI Rival
description: Chat with an AI rival while you play. Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, Groq and more using your own API key (free options included).

connection.name: AI Connection
connection.description:
Pick which AI to use and add your API key.

<cg>Free:</c> Gemini (Google), Groq, OpenRouter's free models, or Ollama on your own PC.
<co>Paid:</c> Claude, ChatGPT, Grok.

The mod page (the <cy>i</c> button) has a step-by-step guide for getting a key from each one. Your key stays on this device and is only sent to the AI you pick.

daily-limit.name: Daily Message Limit
daily-limit.description: Most messages this device sends to the AI per day, so a long session can't run up your bill. <cy>0</c> means no limit.

ai-name.name: AI Name
ai-name.description: Name shown above the AI's speech bubble.

personality-preset.name: Personality
personality-preset.description: <cy>Rival</c>: cocky trash talk. <cy>Coach</c>: hype and tips. <cy>Chill</c>: laid-back friend. <cy>Sarcastic</c>: deadpan narrator. <cy>Grin</c>: a creepy creature living in your screen that gets angrier every time you die, and smashes your screen when it snaps (see <cy>Grin</c> below). <cy>Custom</c>: write your own below.

custom-personality.name: Custom Personality
custom-personality.description: Used when Personality is <cy>Custom</c>. Describe who the AI is and how it talks, up to 1000 characters. Tap <cy>Edit</c> for a big text box; you can paste a prompt you found online. Short replies and no hateful content are always enforced on top.
custom-personality.hint: Who is the AI and how does it talk? Short replies and no hateful content are always added on top.
custom-personality.placeholder: For example: You are Glitch, a robot that speaks in short beeps and gets very excited about wave parts.
examples: You are Glitch, a malfunctioning robot fan of Geometry Dash. You speak in short excited bursts, sometimes add BEEP, and you take every death personally.
You are Grandma Rose, a sweet old lady who has never played a video game. You are confused but very proud of every attempt, and you worry when the player dies a lot.
You are a dramatic sports commentator calling the player's run live, treating every jump like the final of a world championship.
You are the level itself. You are smug about every spike that kills the player and quietly nervous when they get close to the end.

reply-length.name: Reply Length
reply-length.description: How long the AI's replies are. <cy>Very Short</c>: one quick line. <cy>Short</c>: one or two sentences. <cy>Medium</c>: two or three.

memory-size.name: Memory Size
memory-size.description: How many recent messages (yours, the game's and the AI's) are sent along so the AI remembers the run. Memory resets when you enter a new level.

grin-title.name: Grin
grin-title.description: Only used when Personality is Grin.

grin-picture.name: Grin's Look
grin-picture.description: Grin is a 3D creature by default. Pick any <cy>PNG or JPG</c> on your device to use your own picture instead: it becomes the face that smashes your screen, the face on the anger bar and in chat, and the enemy in the fight (tap the middle of it for extra damage). Square pictures work best. Use the reset arrow to go back to the 3D Grin.

rage-bar.name: Anger Bar
rage-bar.description: Shows how angry Grin is in the top-left corner of the level. Deaths fill it: a 1% death on your first tries barely counts, a 90%+ death on an extreme demon counts a lot, and dying at the same spot again and again counts more each time. New bests calm it down a little and beating the level calms it completely.

rage-temper.name: Temper
rage-temper.description: How fast Grin gets angry. <cy>Patient</c> takes much longer to snap, <cy>Short Fuse</c> snaps quickly.

rage-jumpscare.name: Screen Break
rage-jumpscare.description: When the bar fills up, the screen goes dark, Grin roars and smashes your screen from the inside, and it shatters. The level waits until it is over. No flashing lights, but it is a scare: turn it off if you don't want that.

rage-fight.name: Fight Back
rage-fight.description: After the screen breaks, fight Grin in a short mini-game inside your broken screen: tap Grin to hit it (the head hurts more) and shoot it enough to stop its charges before they reach you. Win and its anger drops to zero; lose and it stays angry.

rage-volume.name: Roar Volume
rage-volume.description: Loudness of the roar and the breaking glass.

open-chat.name: Open Chat
open-chat.description: Pauses the level and opens the chat box.

show-ingame-button.name: In-Game Chat Button
show-ingame-button.description: Shows a small chat button next to the pause button while playing. There is always a chat button in the pause menu as well.

auto-reactions.name: Auto Reactions
auto-reactions.description: Let the AI comment on its own when you die, get a new best or beat the level.

react-start.name: On Level Start
react-start.description: Say something when you enter a level.

react-deaths.name: On Deaths
react-deaths.description: Comment on ordinary deaths (with the cooldown and chance below).

react-close-calls.name: On Close Calls
react-close-calls.description: Always comment when you die close to your best.

react-new-best.name: On New Bests
react-new-best.description: Comment when you set a new best.

react-complete.name: On Completion
react-complete.description: Comment when you beat the level.

close-call-range.name: Close Call Range
close-call-range.description: A death within this many percent of your best counts as a close call (once your best is at least 30%).

event-cooldown.name: Death Comment Cooldown
event-cooldown.description: Minimum number of seconds between comments on ordinary deaths. New bests and completions ignore this and are always commented on.

death-reaction-chance.name: Death Comment Chance
death-reaction-chance.description: Chance (in percent) that the AI comments on an ordinary death once the cooldown is over. Close calls near your best are always commented on.

react-in-practice.name: React In Practice Mode
react-in-practice.description: Also comment on deaths and completions in practice mode and when starting from a start position.

note-start.name: Level Start Direction
note-start.description: Extra direction for the AI at this moment, up to 200 characters, for example <cg>Warn me about the wave part.</c>. A level can set its own.
note-start.hint: What should the AI do when you enter a level? Levels can set their own.
note-start.placeholder: For example: Warn me about the hardest part.
examples: Warn me about the hardest part.
Hype me up like it's a boss fight.
Guess how many attempts this will take me.

note-death.name: Death Direction
note-death.description: Extra direction for the AI at this moment, up to 200 characters, for example <cg>Give me a tip instead of roasting me.</c>. A level can set its own.
note-death.hint: What should the AI do when you die? Levels can set their own.
note-death.placeholder: For example: Give me a quick tip instead of roasting me.
examples: Give me a quick tip instead of roasting me.
Count my deaths at the same spot.

note-new-best.name: New Best Direction
note-new-best.description: Extra direction for the AI at this moment, up to 200 characters, for example <cg>Act shocked.</c>. A level can set its own.
note-new-best.hint: What should the AI do when you get a new best? Levels can set their own.
examples: Remind me how far is left.

note-complete.name: Completion Direction
note-complete.description: Extra direction for the AI at this moment, up to 200 characters, for example <cg>Challenge me to do it again faster.</c>. A level can set its own.
note-complete.hint: What should the AI do when you beat the level? Levels can set their own.
note-complete.placeholder: For example: Challenge me to beat it again faster.
examples: Challenge me to beat it again faster.
Act like you knew I could do it all along.

bubble.name: Look & Voice
bubble.description: Where the bubble sits, its size, font, colors and talking sound. Tap <cy>Customize</c> to design it with a live preview: drag the bubble on a mini game screen, pick themes and colors, and replay the reply with its voice.

avatar.name: Icon
avatar.description: The icon next to the AI's name. Tap <cy>Edit</c> to pick a cube and colors from the icon kit, draw your own pixel icon (8 to 32 squares per side), copy your own icon, or turn it off.

chat-look.name: Look
chat-look.description: The chat window's theme, color and size. Tap <cy>Customize</c> to see it live while you change it.

allow-level-config.name: Let Levels Customize The AI
allow-level-config.description: Some levels set their own AI name, personality, look and reactions (see the mod page for how creators do this). Turn off to always use your own settings. Your AI connection, key and limits are never changed by a level.

level-lock.name: Only On Specific Levels
level-lock.description: Only activate the AI on the level IDs listed below.

level-ids.name: Level IDs
level-ids.description: Comma-separated list of level IDs, for example <cg>128, 97354251</c>. Unpublished levels from the editor have ID <cy>0</c>.
